Socioeconomic inequality in an indicator

Source: R/inequality.R
bdhs_inequality.Rd

Computes the standard summary measures of inequality of an indicator across ordered socioeconomic groups (by default household wealth quintiles), with design-based standard errors and confidence intervals, for every round in the data.

Usage

bdhs_inequality(
  data,
  indicator,
  by = NULL,
  measures = .inequality_measures,
  level = 0.95,
  survey = NULL,
  design_args = list()
)

# S3 method for class 'bdhs_inequality'
plot(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bdhs_inequality'
autoplot(object, ...)

Arguments

data

A BDHS recode data frame (one round or pooled rounds).

indicator

A single indicator id (see bdhs_indicator_list()); a proportion or a mean.

by

Ordered grouping variable, lowest group first. NULL (default) uses the harmonized wealth_quintile if present, else v190 (hv270 in household files). Labelled variables are ordered by their codes and factors by their levels.

measures

Measures to compute, any of "difference", "ratio", "sii", "rii", "ci" and "eci".

level

Confidence level.

survey

Optional survey reference, overriding detection.

design_args

A list of further arguments passed to bdhs_design().

x, object

A bdhs_inequality result.

...

Unused.

Value

A tibble of class bdhs_inequality with columns survey_id, indicator, label, by, measure, measure_label, estimate, se, ci_low, ci_high, lowest, highest (labels of the extreme groups) and n_groups.

Details

Let the groups be ordered from poorest (1) to richest (\(K\)), with weighted population shares \(p_k\) in the indicator's denominator population, and let \(R_k = \sum_{j<k} p_j + p_k / 2\) be the weighted ridit (fractional rank) of group \(k\), so that \(R\) runs from 0 (poorest) to 1 (richest).

  • difference: \(\mu_K - \mu_1\) (richest minus poorest group), and ratio: \(\mu_K / \mu_1\). The group means are estimated jointly (survey::svyby() with covmat = TRUE) and the measures with survey::svycontrast() (delta method; the ratio's interval is computed on the log scale).

  • sii, the slope index of inequality: the slope \(\beta\) of the design-based linear regression \(E(y) = \alpha + \beta R\) of the 0/1 outcome on the ridit (survey::svyglm()); the absolute difference between the top and the bottom of the socioeconomic scale (Barros and Victora 2013).

  • rii, the relative index of inequality: \(\exp(\beta)\) from the log-link (quasi-Poisson) regression \(\log E(y) = \alpha + \beta R\), the ratio of the predicted values at the top and the bottom of the scale (Barros and Victora 2013).

  • ci, the concentration index, in its covariance ("convenient regression") form with design weights, \(C = 2\,\mathrm{cov}_w(y, R) / \mu\) (Kakwani, Wagstaff and van Doorslaer 1997; Wagstaff, Paci and van Doorslaer 1991). It is written as a smooth function of survey totals, \(C = 2 T_{yR} / T_y - 2 T_R / N\), and its standard error is obtained by linearization with survey::svycontrast().

  • eci, Erreygers' corrected concentration index for a bounded outcome in \([a, b]\): \(E = 4 \mu C / (b - a) = 8\,\mathrm{cov}_w(y, R)\) for a binary outcome (Erreygers 2009); only for proportions.

Positive values of difference, sii, ci and eci (and ratio, rii above 1) mean that the indicator is higher among the richer. Ridits are treated as fixed (conditional on the observed group shares), as is usual. Proportions are on the 0-100 scale, so difference and sii are in percentage points; the other measures are scale-free.

Indicators with all-women denominators (ratio estimators) get the difference and ratio only. Lonely PSUs are handled with options(survey.lonely.psu = "adjust"), set while the function runs.

References

Barros AJD, Victora CG (2013). Measuring coverage in MNCH: determining and interpreting inequalities in coverage of maternal, newborn, and child health interventions. PLoS Medicine 10(5): e1001390.

Erreygers G (2009). Correcting the concentration index. Journal of Health Economics 28(2): 504-515.

Kakwani N, Wagstaff A, van Doorslaer E (1997). Socioeconomic inequalities in health: measurement, computation, and statistical inference. Journal of Econometrics 77(1): 87-103.

Wagstaff A, Paci P, van Doorslaer E (1991). On the measurement of inequalities in health. Social Science & Medicine 33(5): 545-557.

See also

bdhs_inequality_official() for the same gap measures from the official estimates; bdhs_compare().

Examples

kr <- bdhs_simulate(2022, "KR", n_clusters = 40)
bdhs_inequality(kr, "rh_del_csection")
#> # BDHS inequality: rh_del_csection by v190 | BD2022DHS
#> # A tibble: 6 × 13
#>   survey_id indicator label by    measure measure_label estimate      se  ci_low
#>   <chr>     <chr>     <chr> <chr> <chr>   <chr>            <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 BD2022DHS rh_del_c… Deli… v190  differ… Difference (…   27.2   14.0    -1.67  
#> 2 BD2022DHS rh_del_c… Deli… v190  ratio   Ratio (highe…    3.31   2.22    0.831 
#> 3 BD2022DHS rh_del_c… Deli… v190  sii     Slope index …   35.6   13.7     7.32  
#> 4 BD2022DHS rh_del_c… Deli… v190  rii     Relative ind…    3.30   1.46    1.33  
#> 5 BD2022DHS rh_del_c… Deli… v190  ci      Concentratio…    0.186  0.0672  0.0473
#> 6 BD2022DHS rh_del_c… Deli… v190  eci     Erreygers co…    0.226  0.0900  0.0407
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: ci_high <dbl>, lowest <chr>, highest <chr>,
#> #   n_groups <int>
bdhs_inequality(kr, "rh_del_facility", by = "v106", measures = c("difference", "sii"))
#> # BDHS inequality: rh_del_facility by v106 | BD2022DHS
#> # A tibble: 2 × 13
#>   survey_id indicator    label by    measure measure_label estimate    se ci_low
#>   <chr>     <chr>        <chr> <chr> <chr>   <chr>            <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 BD2022DHS rh_del_faci… Deli… v106  differ… Difference (…     11.3  14.1 -17.8 
#> 2 BD2022DHS rh_del_faci… Deli… v106  sii     Slope index …     27.2  10.9   4.72
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: ci_high <dbl>, lowest <chr>, highest <chr>,
#> #   n_groups <int>
